inclusionRule: Statutes that condition the relationship between citizen and state in a general way or alter fundamental rights, in the sense the courts use when they speak of constitutional statutes, plus the franchise landmarks. Ruled 2026-09-01.
review: Hand-curated. This session had no network access, so the dates and titles here were written from knowledge and have not been checked against primary sources. Spot-check before this ships.

united-kingdom.summary: The United Kingdom has a constitution but not a document. It is a body of statutes, prerogative powers, court decisions and conventions, and any of the statutes can be changed by an ordinary Act of Parliament. That is why the comparative dataset records no amendment procedure for it: there is nothing to amend, only law to replace.

instruments.name: Bill of Rights
instruments.what: Settled the terms on which the Crown holds power: no suspending laws, no taxation without Parliament, free elections, free speech in Parliament.

instruments.name: Act of Settlement
instruments.what: Fixed the succession and gave judges tenure during good behaviour rather than at the Crown's pleasure.

instruments.name: Union with Scotland Act
instruments.what: Merged the English and Scottish parliaments into one Parliament of Great Britain.

instruments.name: Union with Ireland Act
instruments.what: Added Ireland to the union, in force from 1801.

instruments.name: Representation of the People Act
instruments.what: The Great Reform Act: redrew the borough seats and widened the franchise for the first time.

instruments.name: Representation of the People Act
instruments.what: Extended the vote to urban working men, roughly doubling the electorate.

instruments.name: Representation of the People Act
instruments.what: Extended the county franchise on the same terms as the boroughs.

instruments.name: Parliament Act
instruments.what: Removed the Lords' veto over money bills and replaced it with a delaying power.

instruments.name: Representation of the People Act
instruments.what: Near-universal male suffrage and the vote for women over 30 with a property qualification.

instruments.name: Representation of the People (Equal Franchise) Act
instruments.what: Equalised the franchise at 21 for women and men.

instruments.name: Statute of Westminster
instruments.what: Ended Westminster's power to legislate for the dominions without their request.

instruments.name: Parliament Act
instruments.what: Cut the Lords' delaying power from two years to one.

instruments.name: Life Peerages Act
instruments.what: Created appointed life peers, remaking the composition of the second chamber.

instruments.name: Representation of the People Act
instruments.what: Lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.

instruments.name: European Communities Act
instruments.what: Gave European law effect in the United Kingdom and priority over inconsistent domestic law.

instruments.name: Human Rights Act
instruments.what: Made Convention rights enforceable in domestic courts and required legislation to be read compatibly where possible.

instruments.name: Scotland Act
instruments.what: Created the Scottish Parliament and defined what is reserved to Westminster.

instruments.name: Government of Wales Act
instruments.what: Created the National Assembly for Wales.

instruments.name: Northern Ireland Act
instruments.what: Put the Belfast Agreement into law and created the Assembly and the power-sharing executive.

instruments.name: House of Lords Act
instruments.what: Removed all but 92 hereditary peers from the Lords.

instruments.name: Constitutional Reform Act
instruments.what: Separated the top court from the Lords, creating the Supreme Court, and reformed the Lord Chancellor's role.

instruments.name: Fixed-term Parliaments Act
instruments.what: Took the power to call an early election out of the Prime Minister's hands. Repealed in 2022.

instruments.name: European Union (Withdrawal) Act
instruments.what: Repealed the 1972 Act and converted retained EU law into domestic law.

instruments.name: European Union (Withdrawal Agreement) Act
instruments.what: Gave effect to the withdrawal agreement and the transition period.

instruments.name: Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act
instruments.what: Restored the prerogative power to dissolve Parliament.

new-zealand.summary: New Zealand is the other pure case: no single constitutional document, no upper house since 1950, and a Bill of Rights that courts may interpret around but cannot use to strike down a statute.

instruments.name: New Zealand Constitution Act
instruments.what: Passed at Westminster, it created representative government and the provinces.

instruments.name: Maori Representation Act
instruments.what: Created four seats reserved for Maori voters.

instruments.name: Electoral Act
instruments.what: Gave women the vote, the first country in the world to do so in a national election.

instruments.name: Statute of Westminster Adoption Act
instruments.what: Took up the independence the 1931 Statute offered.

instruments.name: Legislative Council Abolition Act
instruments.what: Abolished the upper house, leaving a unicameral Parliament.

instruments.name: Treaty of Waitangi Act
instruments.what: Created the Waitangi Tribunal to hear claims under the Treaty.

instruments.name: Constitution Act
instruments.what: Repealed the 1852 Act and gathered the core rules of government into one statute.

instruments.name: New Zealand Bill of Rights Act
instruments.what: Set out civil and political rights, without the power to strike down legislation.

instruments.name: Electoral Act
instruments.what: Replaced first past the post with mixed-member proportional representation, after a referendum.

instruments.name: Supreme Court Act
instruments.what: Ended appeals to the Privy Council and created a domestic Supreme Court.

united-states.label: The Organic Laws of the United States
united-states.summary: Every edition of the United States Code opens with four documents, not one. They are printed together as the Organic Laws, and the Constitution is the last of them rather than the whole of them.
united-states.context: Placed against the rest of the world: the oldest national constitution still in force, shorter than all but 27 of the 191 codified constitutions on record, and amended at 0.7 events per decade, which is roughly a tenth of Brazil's rate.

documents.name: Declaration of Independence
documents.what: Stated the principles the new country claimed for itself: consent of the governed, and a right to alter a government that withholds it.

documents.name: Articles of Confederation
documents.what: The first national compact. Drafted 1777, in force 1781, and abandoned in 1789 for want of a workable federal power.

documents.name: Northwest Ordinance
documents.what: Governed the Northwest Territory and set the terms on which new states could join as equals rather than as possessions.

documents.name: Constitution of the United States
documents.what: Adopted 1787, in force 1789, amended 27 times in 16 separate acts. The oldest national constitution still in force anywhere.
